tl;dr: This image is entirely bullshit.

  • Unemployment rate: He said one estimate put it at astronomical levels. This analysis is extremely speculative and , and Trump sums it up by giving a percentage of unemployment. The amount of hours people could work but don't does not count as unemployment. Politifact got it right, albeit they did exaggerate a bit with "pants on fire".

  • "They send the bad ones over": Ad hominem attack. If it's so biased to be untruthful then it's easy to refute. I cannot comment on the article in question as I can't read Spanish but I'm going to assume that if the Mexican government purposefully sent criminals over the border it wouldn't just be in one publication.

  • 30 million illegal immigrants: He quoted a guy. That doesn't mean the statement is untruthful. Being a former Mexican ambassador doesn't make it true.

  • Negative GDP: Unless the omitted portion of his quote was "growth", he said something stupid. He conflated GDP with GDP growth. Sure, the amount of production in a country can't be negative, but the topic he refers to is GDP growth which has been negative. Hyperbole doesn't even come into the picture here.

  • Kuwait: The war cost $61 billion and a coalition of nations from all around the world (Saudi Arabia and Kuwait being the primary contributors of around $16 each) ponied up $54 billion. This would be unacceptable IF the US armed forces are a mercenary force. This is not the case. This war was not intended to be a venture for profit; the US decided to intervene in the region and other sympathizing countries decided to support the venture financially.

  • CNN poll: Trump is technically correct in that CNN reported on a poll in which this was the case. However, he insisted this was a "recent" poll, while in reality it was in February 2011. His numbers nosedived after his participation in the birth certificate fiasco and he never again reached those numbers in that election cycle. I don't doubt he would be leading by far in a poll conducted today against Obama but there's really no point in wasting resources on a poll for a hypothetical that can't happen. I think Politifact got it right but embellished the offense with "pants on fire".
